summary:
A web-based interactive jukebox that pairs NASA Earth Information Center visualizations with real-time dynamic sonifications generated from decoded physical data values.
The project addresses a common limitation of scientific visualizations: while satellite images and maps communicate environmental changes visually, they are not always accessible or intuitive to everyone. Earth Information Jukebox bridges this gap by translating scientific measurements into meaningful musical experiences.

The platform uses NASA Earth observation resources, particularly NASA Global Imagery Browse Services (GIBS), to retrieve historical satellite imagery and environmental datasets covering 2004–2024.

Instead of directly converting image brightness or pixel colours into sound, the project attempts to reconstruct the actual scientific measurements represented by those colours. A Python-based processing pipeline retrieves NASA GIBS equirectangular imagery, parses XML colormap specifications, and uses KD-tree colour matching to map image pixels back to their corresponding physical measurements. The recovered data is then downsampled to a 180 × 90 grid and translated into musical parameters using pentatonic scales. Tone.js is used to generate dynamic soundscapes based on the processed environmental data.

The project currently focuses on three primary soundscapes. Ocean Fever uses GHRSST MUR sea surface temperature data to translate ocean temperature variations into musical patterns
details:
I chose Earth Jukebox because the idea of turning images of Earth into music really caught my teams attention. Normally, when we look at NASA's data, we just see images, graphs, and numbers. But I found it interesting that we could actually turn those visuals into sounds and experience them in a completely different way.

What I liked most was that we're not just making music, we're trying to give Earth's data a voice. I feel this could be a really interesting way to help people connect with and understand our planet better. , by using more senses than just vision and touch
